articleTitle: Heritage Tourism and Religious Identity: A Deep Neural Network-Based Deductive Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the classification of Southeast Asian temples with the deep neural network with various images of temples. Two of the most popular Buddhist temples in Thailand are Wat Prakaew and Wat Po. The stunning temples in Thailand draw tens of thousands of visitors every year. Sadly, many tourists to the temple sometimes cannot tell whether their vacation photographs were taken at Wat Prakaew or Wat Po. In this study, we use deep learning and computer vision to identify whether a given photograph was shot at Wat Prakaew or Wat Po. The idea is to use a deep neural network to create a pattern that makes it easy to classify images. The work shows better classification results compared to other machine-learning techniques. The proposed techniques attain 96.33% validation accuracy.

articleTitle: Waste Management Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the modern world waste pollution is the challenging environmental issues. To reduce pollution, we need to recycle the waste. In order to recycle waste, one must know which category the waste belongs to. Waste classification is a social issue related to people’s livelihood, so letting smart systems perform intelligent waste classification has important significance. So, we are here with a waste detection system that uses deep learning and categorizes the waste plastic or non-recyclable or glass or bio or others. The proposed system is trained and tested to detect the classify the waste using the CNN(Convolution Neural Network) i.e. a deep learning algorithm. The image of the waste material is fed into a neural network which determines the class of object. We have considered precision, recall and F1 Score as performance metrics to evaluate our model. The proposed model is compared with existing baseline models like machine learning, basic neural networks and datamining approach. The developed deep learning model has outperformed the existing literature with chosen parameters.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection using Cellular Automata Based Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Fake News detection is one of the concerns of the modern era. We have many mechanisms to identify the fake news from various sources. Still there is a need of a precise and more adoptable tool to predict the fake news. In this paper we have introduced the theoretical structure of the proposed classifier (DEEP LEARNING-CA) with implementation. We have augmented hybrid cellular automata with RNN (Recurrent Neural Networks) for designing a novel classifier. We have collected the datasets from Mendeley data & trained & tested our classifier. Deep Learning-CA reports an accuracy of 90.18% which outperforms some of the existing base line classifiers. We have used various parameters precision, recall, f-measure and ROC to compare our research with our existing baseline methods.

articleTitle: A Context Sensitive with Effective Task Migration in Mobile Cloud Computing Services
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Cloud computing has gained popularity in recent years and is modernizing the internet computer architecture. Mobile applications and gadgets are also rapidly transforming. As the acceptance and functionality of mobile devices have increased recently, Mobile Cloud Computing (MCC) has attracted a lot of research interest. As mobile technologies progress, new compute-intensive tasks are quickly appearing. On mobile devices, though, these tasks are challenging to complete due to resource restrictions. By conducting an operation in the cloud and then transmitting the result to the user's mobile device, cloud transportation is utilised to solve this issue. A prototype MCC offloading system used in this analysis offers an adaptable MCC service that takes into consideration a variety of cloud services, including mobile ad-hoc networks, cloudlets, and public clouds. They describe a context-aware offloading with effective cloud migration decision making algorithm in this analysis, with the goal of providing code offloading decisions and compute-intensive tasks at runtime on selecting wireless medium and which potential cloud resources as the offloading location based on the device context. Whether a function is on a cloud server or a mobile device depends on the decision-making process around its transfer. Also examined how well mobile and cloud execution performed, demonstrating how using a cloud server can speed up task execution. To evaluate the effectiveness of the presented algorithm, they also run actual experiments on the system that has been put into place. Based on the various mobile device contexts, the system and embedded decision algorithm are able to select suitable wireless mediums and cloud resources, resulting in a significant performance boost, according to the findings.In this case, the presented algorithm will outperform other approaches in terms of execution time and energy consumption in this analysis.

articleTitle: Automated Brain Tumor Detection Using Soft Computing-Based Segmentation Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Development and growth of abnormal cells within the brain results in brain tumor. In this study, a novel segmentation methodology is proposed for the segmentation of tumor. The proposed model consists of two phases. In the first phase, the brain CT image from the medical database is pre-processed to remove artifacts and noise. For Image segmentation, a Hierarchical Self Organizing Map (HSOM) is used that provides promising segmentation results. The conformist Self Organizing Map (SOM), which was used to categorize the picture row by row, is extended by the HSOM. Thus, the HSOM with vector quantization speeds up calculation at this lowest level of the weight vector, where there are more tumor pixels. The proposed automated system is tested on Kaggle (online available) database and achieves an accuracy of 98.94%.

articleTitle: Diabetic Macular Edema Detection based on Non-mydriatic Retinal Image
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) is an advanced stage of diabetic retinopathy where the microaneurysms from the retinal vessels may leak fluid or blood into macula the central part of retina. This may cause serious damage to the eyes which may eventually lead to blindness. Therefore, determining the stages of DME is an open research problem. In this work, we proposed a deep learning-based method to identify DME with grading based on non-mydriatic retinal fundus images. We applied multiple image augmentation techniques, such as cropping, resizing, and flipping. Then the preprocessed images were used to train convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model to detect DME and determine the level of grading: Grade 0, Grade 1, and Grade 2. We trained and tested our model using multiple pre-trained CNNs i.e., AlexNet, ResNet18, ResNet34, DenseNet121, DenseNet161, VGG11_bn, VGG16_bn, SqueezeNet, and Inception. Out of all the models VGG16 showed the best accuracy of 96%, sensitivity of 95.8%, and specificity of 96.9%. A comparison against the state-of-the-art methods for DME staging prediction from non-mydriatic images reveal that our approach outperformed the existing methods. The proposed model was developed for non- mydriatic images collected the from IDRID dataset which makes it suitable for its application in clinics lacking proper ophthalmology facilities as well as in remote area lacking a proper ophthalmology clinic.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Speech Disorder using FOA-SCNet
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Speech disorders have turned out a great brunt on the ability of speech. The persons have speech disorders were struggling with communication and emotional expressions. The proposed work detects and classifies the speech disorders using combined CNN and SVM techniques. To improve the prediction accuracy of the proposed model, we use the Fruitfly optimization algorithm for improving the convergence rate and accuracy results. The study mainly focuses on young people in which the speech disorders are prevalent. The machine algorithm is utilized to predict a person has healthy or pathological voice accurately.

articleTitle: FinTech Usage in Saudi Arabia: The implications on youth financial decisions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Financial technology (FinTech) applications have become an integral part of our lives, and one of the most affected sectors is the economic sector. The majority of FinTech users in Saudi Arabia are young people who are under 35 years old. However, little is known about their FinTech usage and its impact on their financial decisions. In this work-in-progress, we aim to explore how young Saudis utilize FinTech applications to manage their finances, with particular attention to a specified special category of those users (e.g., the beneficiaries of university stipends, social funds, etc.). We use a descriptive qualitative research design to answer the research questions. The results will be analyzed in light of the UTAUT model. The results can assist academics, policymakers, and young people in understanding the relationship between their FinTech use and money management practices.

articleTitle: SemCom for Metaverse: Challenges, Opportunities and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Metaverse is a new paradigm yet to come, gaining popularity in many applications and being developed using a combination of technologies, including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), blockchain, and other immersive technologies. One key technology critical to the success of the Metaverse is Semantic Communication (SemCom), which enables efficient and effective communication between humans and intelligent agents. This paper discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with SemCom in the Metaverse and potential future trends. We identify the critical challenges in SemCom, such as context awareness, scalability, and interoperability, and discuss potential solutions to address these challenges. Furthermore, we explore the various opportunities that SemCom can bring to the Metaverse, such as improved user experiences, interactions with virtual assistants, and enhanced data analysis capabilities. Moreover, we examine the emerging trends in SemCom for the Metaverse and highlight some key research directions that will be important in the future.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Based Human Emotion Recognition using EEG brain signals
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In daily lives, human experience a different emotion i.e.- sadness, angry, happiness. and rage that are very closely related tits behavior and play an important role in their daily routines. Emotion recognition means that identify and classify the human emotional mind state using their EEG brain signal, because EEG is very convenient and gives necessary information about brain emotion state. Since, emotion recognition through EEG signals is an active and challenging research area due to the non-stationary behavior of the signal. Therefore, Fastest, and accurate method is essential for automatically recognize and classify the human emotions. In this paper, we proposed RNN based Emotion Recognition model which consist of different layers i.e.- input layer, Dense layer, flatten layer, ReLU layer, SoftMax layer, and dropout layer that are used for feature extraction and model classification. ADAM optimization algorithm is used for model training which update the parameters of network after each iteration of epoch. EEG signals are used to train, validate and to predict the brain state of the human. The training accuracy of proposed model is 96.25% with 0.01 learning rate. To show the robustness and efficiency of proposed model, we compared with similar studies that shows performance of the proposed algorithm is better than the existing one in terms of better classification and model accuracy.

articleTitle: Detecting Cross-site Scripting Attacks using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The most frequently encountered attack in web applications is known as Cross-site Scripting (XSS). This type of attack is designed to compromise the sensitive information of users, and there exist three distinct types of XSS attacks. The main challenge to detect XSS, was that the attackers changes XSS pattern frequently. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was proposed as an appropriate model for classifying XSS. Here a CNN model with Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) was proposed and tested as XSS detector model. We developed a methodology to train the CNN and generate training dataset using GAN. The proposed model is suited for XSS classification, it achieved 99.4% of precision, 99.3% of recall and 99.4 of accuracy. The proposed model was compared with other three deep learning methods and it achieved better performance in overall.

articleTitle: Synthetic Randomized Image Augmentation (SRIA) to Address Class Imbalance Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: With emerging deep learning technologies, the issue of class imbalance has become more relevant specially for object detection problem as performance of modern object detectors is more likely to suffer from class imbalance than traditional machine learning methods. Foreground-foreground class imbalance particularly affects deep learning models when trained from dataset following real world data distribution. To bridge this gap, this work overviews the limitations and capabilities of existing techniques to balance classes and proposes synthetic randomized image augmentation (SRIA) technique to address the class imbalance problem. The proposed technique comprises of two steps. First, objects from minority class training image are extracted using weak learning and subsequently new minority class images are synthesized by leveraging background substitution and data augmentation. We evaluate the proposed technique on state-of-the-art object detector i.e Yolov5 which shows performance improvement by 5% when compared with vanilla model trained on imbalanced data.

articleTitle: Natural disasters detection and classification based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: With the technological development that we are witnessing at all times, and the height of the spread of artificial intelligence in life, all fields have become dependent on it to solve problems. In recent years, most countries have perceived large natural disasters in a very harmful way, including floods and fires, and they sometimes spread to residential areas. These disasters caused great damage from suffocation, burns, drownings, deaths, and others, or take safety precautions. Therefore, in the interest of the safety of the environment and people, and taking advantage of the advantages of artificial intelligence, we proposed the idea of detecting disasters, protecting the environment, and preserving people's lives so that safety measures are taken. The proposed system detects the presence of disaster after image processing and then classified it if it is flood or fire based on Convolutional Neural Network. We achieved an excellent accuracy rate of 99.77% compared with other state of art works.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach of Image Retrieving In Biometric ID
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The process of storing and retrieving information is crucial, and storing it in a coded manner makes it safe and ensures that the mechanism of storage and retrieval technique is practical and straightforward. This research proposes a DNA computing-based practical technique for encryption, auto-storing, and auto-retrieval. It uses an HDC-HP (Hybrid DNA Computing and Hypernetwork) approach. The properties of the graph may be used to identify the various locations in the memory where information is stored, and a decent means of even encrypting and storing information is discovered. Compared to other storage media, DNA is far more powerful and supports highly parallel processing. Consider a few fascinating issues that have applications in both theoretical and practical disciplines to aid physicists, scientists, mathematicians, chemists, biologists, etc. This work uses the benefits of DNA computing and graph theory to store and retrieve data more securely and effectively. With a retrieval accuracy of 98.7%, the HDC- HP method produced an exceptional result.

articleTitle: Am I Safe? Understanding Saudi Women Rideshare Drivers Safety Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Ridesharing is part of the gig economy and is growing at significant rates. Safety in ridesharing is a necessity for both riders and drivers. However, previous research focused more on the riders’ perspective while overlooking the safety of the driver. Since in Saudi Arabia, females were recently allowed to drive and therefore are generally less experienced compared to the male population, we decided to investigate the female drivers’ safety. In this work-in-progress, we interview three female rideshare drivers in Saudi Arabia and ask them about their safety perspectives. The drivers shared that they generally feel safe on the road. However, certain conditions contribute to their lack of feelings of safety such as: limited safety training for drivers, passengers’ ability to abuse the rideshare app features, and lack of technical support. The participants also suggested design features that can improve their safety.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Sentiment Analysis on Twitter Data with LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Sentiment analysis, also known as opinion mining, aims to categorize subjective information in texts into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments. It involves analyzing words to determine emotions expressed in sentences, paragraphs, or documents. The process includes cleaning the text by removing unnecessary characters, stop words, and punctuation, as well as tokenization to divide the text into separate words while maintaining contextual meaning. Analyzing sentiment in Twitter data requires extensive preprocessing, including the removal of unnecessary characters, handling hashtags, and tokenization. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), a type of recurrent neural network, is an effective technique for sentiment analysis as it captures sequential and contextual information from text data. In this study, an LSTM model is proposed to perform sentimental analysis on Twitter data. The proposed model was able to achieve 93% accuracy with 0.93 F1 score, outperforming other models.

articleTitle: Multiclass X-Ray Image Classification Using Transfer Learning Based Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In recent past years, the world has been surprised and troubled by the novel coronavirus and its impact on all the fields of life. The coronavirus is a very complex structure difficult to understand and till now it’s growing with new mutations. The virus is very contagious and has affected over 80% of the world's population. Several approaches have been tried for detecting COVID-19, including RT-PCR, however, they are both intrusive and inaccurate. Using radiography in conjunction with a radiologist's expertise is a viable alternative method for detecting COVID-19. To avoid the drawbacks of employing chest X-rays for COVID-19 detection, deep learning methods may be utilized instead. A pre-trained neural network can detect the presence of the virus in chest X-rays by looking for certain viral patterns. X-rays may be analyzed for these patterns to determine if a sample is COVID-positive or -negative, pneumonia-related, or otherwise normal. In this article, we use a neural network that has been pre-trained with 5800 X-ray pictures labeled as covid, pneumonia, or normal in order to identify COVID and pneumonia. The model's performance was evaluated using the following metrics: accuracy (98.50%), precision (98.5), recall (98.34), and F1-Score. The proposed model is compared with another pre-trained model and it outperforms.

articleTitle: Heritage of India: Advanced Monuments Classification using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Tourism is India's most lucrative service industry. Many historical buildings and cultural practices originated in India. Every year, millions of people go to tourist hotspots, and millions more share photos they have taken there on social media and mobile devices with friends and family. The promotion and dissemination of cultural assets as well as tourism activities and landmarks in urban settings might benefit greatly from the use of artificial intelligence methods and machine learning algorithms, which are already being used in a wide variety of settings. Automatic identification and categorization of landmarks and tourist attractions might be an intriguing use case for these methods in the cultural and touristic sector. This study makes an effort to categorize India's historic sites. Hotels, travel companies, restaurants, government organizations, etc. all benefit from the classification of monuments so that they may better plan for the future and provide facilities that are up to date with visitor expectations. Using a deep learning technique, the suggested approach aims to retrieve characteristics and categorize the Indian landmarks that visitors visited.

articleTitle: PDF Malware Detection optimisation using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Initial penetration is an essential technique for launching corporate cyberattacks. In most cases, such invasions result in the loss of private and sensitive data. Because email communication is vital in day-to-day business activity, attackers generally use email as an attack vector to accomplish early penetration of the targeted firm. Emails allow the attacker to deliver malicious files or links to malicious websites. Attackers use social engineering to induce victims to open malicious emails, download files, or click links. Recent assaults often attach non-executable files since existing company defences restrict executables from accessing corporate networks via emails, particularly PDF files. Therefore, there is a high demand for a method that can identify malicious PDF files, as embedded malware in PDFs is a significant hazard to all users nowadays. For many years, static and dynamic processing have been used in malware detection. It employs machine learning techniques to reduce manual input and optimise processing time. In this work, we apply machine learning techniques and multiple machine learning methodologies to identify dangerous programs and evaluate the accuracy of the acquired findings. We obtained greater accuracy when compared to the related studies.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Detection of Digital Face Video Manipulation using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Digital face manipulation and classification have recently attracted the attention of academia and industry worldwide. Researchers have developed deep learning and computer vision techniques for detecting face manipulations, and it has become a challenging task to differentiate between authentic and manipulated face images manually. The challenge results in the decline of authenticity in digital media content. In this paper, we propose a framework for the classification of manipulating face images using the EfficientNet learning model. The proposed framework takes four digital facial forgeries: Face-Swap, Face-2-Face, DeepFakes, and neural textures. Multiple manipulation techniques are used to process manipulated faces, such as the Blaze-face tracking method, to determine the locations of the face images and pixel coordinates. The proposed framework is used first to identify the type of face manipulation and then to perform detection of the tampered regions in the face images. The proposed framework provided an automated benchmark that considers all four modification techniques in a realistic situation. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing approaches regarding accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed framework is suitable for detecting digital face video manipulation in various applications, including forensics and security.

articleTitle: Power Management in Solar PV System with Battery Protection by using MATLAB Simulink
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: It is a clearly known fact that solar energy as a renewable form of energy is the cleanest energy in the world and its utilization has a widespread applications and various industries as well as residential in many places. A major challenge to the usage of solar energy is the unavailability of sunlight in the night and/low irradiation during some hours of the day or during some season such as in the winter. In order to overcome this challenge, there is the need to store excess solar energy generated during the day and make use of it when needed. This solar energy can thus be stored in a storage unit called battery. There is need for battery protection and control or to protect the battery from harm, effective protection scheme is required for the PV-battery-load system. This work presents a PV-Battery Storage-Load system design with control system for protection of the system and also discuss the model and determines the PV system rated power through simulation using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Knee Osteoarthritis Detection And Classification Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a common disease that causes pain, stiffness, and decreased mobility by wearing down the cartilage between the bones in the knee joint. Early and automatic detection of knee OA is important for ensuring effective treatment for patients. The aim of this article is to develop a deep learning model using ResNet50 architecture for the accurate classification of knee osteoarthritis (OA) from images of X-rays originally labeled using the Kellgren–Lawrence (KL) Scale. The dataset used in the current study involves images taken from 4796 participants of ages between 45 and 79 years, with approximately nine thousand knee X-ray images. The ResNet50 model is trained on this dataset, and various evaluation metrics were used to evaluate its performance. A flask-based web application was also developed for using the trained model. Our model achieved a high degree of accuracy (97.4%) in classifying knee OA, suggesting that it could be a valuable tool for diagnosing this condition quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Automatic Recognition of Arabic Poetry Meter Using Machine Learning, Template Matching, and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper discusses three methods to identify the Arabic poetry meter; namely: Machine Learning (ML), Template Matching (TM), and Deep Learning (DL). The Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) features were extracted. The MFCC features are used to represent the spectrogram and frequency domains, then they are used with ML, TM, and DL models. In TM, the following methods /algorithms are used: the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) and Oriented FAST, rotated BRIEF (ORB), and a type of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)- which is the VGG16 deep learner. The final results show that ML outperforms other methods (TM, and DL) with an overall accuracy of 92.2%. The results are promising for auto recognition of the Arabic poetry meter -which is important for Arabic poetry learning.

articleTitle: K-means and Principal Components Analysis Approach For Clustering Malicious URLs
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Security flaws in the world of cyber security are a major concern with the advancement of internet technologies. Malicious URLs are increasing with the number of web links in the world. Developing techniques to classify blacklisted malicious URLs is one of the most focused solutions in the security community. In this paper, we developed a clustering approach to find the similarity into different malicious URLs.The effectiveness of our technique was evaluated using the ISCX-URL-2016 data set, which contains over 110,000 URLs. The collection of necessary features group data is included in the ISCX-URL-2016 data set. Therefore, the data were prepossessed and scaled, then two most commonly used lightweight algorithms are implemented: k-means and principal component analysis. Experimental results exhibit by combining the two algorithms has produced several evaluation results of identifying new potential attack categorizes.

articleTitle: Synergistic Human-Computer/Robot Integration in Multifaceted Business Decision-Making Processes: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of AI techniques has transformed decision-making by integrating AI and human intelligence within organizations. AI algorithms, combined with human talent, enhance decision-making by recognizing influential factors and adapting to complex situations. They have become essential different industries such as banking, healthcare, retail, supply chain, and transportation, enabling faster, objective, and cost-effective decisions. However, concerns about data privacy and algorithmic bias arise. This paper introduces the Throughput Model, a unique decision-making framework, integrating perception, information, judgment, and decision choice. It highlights the role of AI algorithms across industries and their alignment with the model under investigation. AI-powered algorithms enhance decision-making, increasing productivity and customer satisfaction. The paper suggests more research to evaluate the model's performance, address bias, explore human-AI collaboration, and optimize practical implementation.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of a Versatile Dataset of Speech, Real and Synthesized, of Arabic Learners
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Computer-Aided Pronunciation Training (CAPT) systems are gaining popularity recently due to the advancements in deep neural networks (DNN) and machine learning and the availability of databases of speech of language learners. Unfortunately, research in Arabic CAPT systems suffer from the lack of CAPT datasets compared to other languages. In this paper, we present the details of and the ideas used in the development of a versatile dataset of speech, real and synthesized, of Arabic Learners. To develop the dataset, we utilized an existing Arabic speech corpus, King Saud University Speech Database (KSU-SD). KSU-SD's main application was a speaker recognition system, but it was designed to be useful in other applications such as CAPT systems. KSU-SD includes a large number of speakers from diverse nationalities (Saudis, Arabs, and Non-Arabs). KSU-SD contains the recording of about 60 non-native speakers from more than 20 nationalities, hence we selected it to build the non-native Arabic-CAPT corpus. The developed corpus consists of transcribed, segmented, and annotated speech, which makes it suitable for building Arabic CAPT systems. In addition to presenting the details of developing the dataset, we also present an analysis of the text and speech errors of the dataset. The dataset was verified by many CAPT systems.

articleTitle: Design of Real-Time Vision-Based Face Verification and Tracking Via Pan Tilt Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Computer vision and autonomous systems are sub-fields of artificial intelligence. Vision-based applications are significantly applied in surveillance, healthcare, and assistance fields. Pan Tilt Camera is assembled and implemented in the proposed system. The face verification stage in Pan Tilt-based face tracking system is processed using One-Shot Encoding models. The study indicates the implementation of two encoding models, Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) encoding models. The locomotion algorithm is based on a sequence of arithmetical equations. The CNN encoding model performance shows more accurate verification values, whereas HOG encoding model performance shows less accurate verification values. The HOG encoding model-based tracking performance shows highly accurate, streamlined, and rapid locomotion- behavior, whereas the CNN encoding model-based tracking performance shows less accurate, inefficient, and slow locomotion-behavior.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Effects on Chest X-ray Images for COVID-19 Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has affected all aspects of healthcare in the world with infection rates increasing exponentially. The detection process that has been carried out so far through Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) examination, has a low level of accuracy, examination time, and sensitivity. Detecting COVID-19 can also be accomplished through the utilization of radiographic images like chest X-rays (CXR) and Computed Tomography (CT) with a higher level of accuracy and a fast examination time. By implementing deep learning as a predictive method for detecting COVID-19, results can be obtained quickly with a better level of accuracy. However, in its development, not many studies have analyzed the impact of improving image quality, which has considerable influence on the accuracy of the image data tested. Therefore, this research was conducted to analyze the results of testing the transfer learning model of COVID-19 images and normal images using the images quality has improved through the image-enhancement process. The image enhancements used in the research are Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and Unsharp Masking (UM). Then, the improved quality images are trained with pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) methods, ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B4. By using the images that have been improved using CLAHE, the accuracy which obtained in the ResNet34 model are 77%, and 90% with the EfficientNet model, respectively. Furthermore, the results on testing images that have been enhanced using the UM method obtained 81% accuracy on the ResNet34 model, and 96% on the EfficientNet-B4 model, respectively.

articleTitle: Work-in-Progress: Investigating intention to use virtual environments using Technology Readiness Index: A quantitative study in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Past studies have confirmed that virtual environments play a critical aspect in performing daily tasks. Investigating users’ readiness to use this technology while incorporating social presence and immersion is scarce. In this study, we will focus on Saudi users and their readiness to use virtual environments in business settings. Building on the theoretical lenses of the technology readiness index, UTAUT2, social presence, and immersion, we propose a research model to investigate Saudi users’ readiness to use virtual environments. Particularly, we aim to understand end-users’ readiness to adopt and use virtual environments in business settings. This work could stipulate a better understanding about users’ tendency to use and embrace virtual environments technology in Saudi organizations.

articleTitle: FindLoc: A Sentiment Analysis-Based Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: A recommendation system (RS) is a tool for filtering information that attempts to recommend interesting items. Globally, RS is based on analyzing users’ preferences and their implicit or explicit evaluations of items. Searching for a good doctor, restaurant, school, dentist, cafeteria, etc., in real-time from the user's current location remains challenging in Algeria. In order to facilitate the finding of interesting locations for Algerian users, we propose in this work a collaborative recommendation system called FindLoc that learns to classify the different places according to their distances and previous users’ evaluations. First, we gathered users' evaluations (ratings and comments) on various locations in Guelma city. Then, a sentiment analysis method is applied to analyze the dataset and distinguish positive from negative opinions. Then, a recommendation algorithm is proposed to recommend interesting locations based on four parameters: the location (longitude and latitude), previous item ratings, users' comments, and users' ages. Real users evaluated the system, and we obtained very encouraging results in terms of precision, which was 0.91.

articleTitle: A Jaccard Factor-Based Heuristic for the Set k-Cover Problem in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The applications of a wireless sensor network rely heavily on the network’s ability to function for an extended period. By separating the sensors into groups, each of which may keep an eye on the entire area of interest and be activated alternately, the system’s lifetime can be maximized. However, determining the most significant number of different sensor covers necessitates solving the NP-complete set k-cover issue. This work presents an improved greedy approach to the set k-cover problem based on the Jaccard Similarity Coefficient. The latter is a statistical method used to understand the similarity and diversity between sample sets. Moreover, the quality of the produced solution is improved by removing duplicate sensors for each set cover. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was compared to some greedy-based methods from the literature based on 1000 widely used benchmark instances. Computational results demonstrate its efficacy in producing high-quality solutions within acceptable computational time, especially when the problem scale increases

articleTitle: Incorporating Eye-Tracking and Facial Expression Recognition for Preference Prediction in Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Human behavior contains significant information that can greatly contribute to improving the way we interact with computer systems. Getting a better understanding of a user during their interaction with a computer system will greatly improve usability and user satisfaction. Current recommender systems lack such human behavioral indicators. Adding these indicators can be a valuable factor in improving typical recommender systems. This paper proposed a framework that incorporates behavioral indicators in recommender systems to predict user preference. The behavioral indicators chosen for this framework are eye-tracking and emotion recognition through facial expressions.

articleTitle: Classification of Fruit Images as Fresh and Rotten Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Many fruits are produced all over the world, and the fruits produced are sent abroad and sold in a relatively short time in many countries. During the period between collection and sale, the fruits may undergo various types of spoilage. In many cases, the fruits go through a number of fabrication processes for sale. If the fruits comply with certain standards after passing the quality tests at the factory, for example, if the fruits have not started to rot, shipment can begin. In this study, we consider the problem of detecting any type of rot/mold as a binary classification problem. To train and test different convolutional neural network models, we have collected a dataset using images of rotting /spoiled and fresh fruits. Different deep-learning models have been implemented and tested to solve this problem. In this study, the ResNet50 network architecture with real-time data augmentation obtained the best results. Our experimental results show that the ResNet50 model can solve this problem with an accuracy of around 90%.

articleTitle: Hybrid Model Representation in Process Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Process mining is an effective approach for organizations to better understand their end-to-end processes. There are two main types of the process modeling languages: procedural and declarative in process mining. However, a hybrid model can be created by combining both the procedural and declarative modeling languages. Procedural modeling languages can be ineffective to manage with a large number of different exceptions. Declarative modeling languages are easier to manage as they simply encode a set of constraints on the process behavior. Both modeling languages have strengths and weaknesses. The hybrid model was introduced by combining Petro nets and Declare to overcome some of the weaknesses of the procedural and declarative modeling languages. However, more real-life applications are required with different languages.

articleTitle: Arctan Inverse Weibull Distribution: Estimation, Simulation and Application
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In this study, we introduce the arctan inverse Weibull (AIW) distribution, which is an extension of the inverse Weibull (IW) distribution. The AIW distribution is more flexible than other well-known statistical models, and it includes several sub-models. We computed the AIW distribution’s statistical features such as quantile function, median, skewness, kurtosis, inverse moments, harmonic mean (HM) and order statistics. The model parameters were determined using the maximum likelihood (ML) approach. A Monte Carlo simulation study is described to evaluate the effectiveness of the ML technique for calculating AIW distribution parameters. To demonstrate the significance of the AIW distribution, we implemented it to an actual dataset of current interest: COVID-19 death cases recorded in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) from 14 April to 22 June 2020. The new suggested model gives better fit more than other competitive models for the dataset.

articleTitle: Dark Vision Assistive Application for Deaf-Blind People
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: For visually impaired, deaf-blind people, both communication and navigation are difficult activities and indoor navigation is becoming increasingly harder for them. It is even more difficult for deaf-blind people than it is for non-visually impaired people. People with visual impairments or deaf- blindness frequently rely on external support systems to make judgments, such as trained canines, humans, or specialized equipment. As a result, deaf-blind people are in desperate need of an assistive application that allows blind people to navigate and communicate freely without relying on others. The goal of the application is to create a more adaptable and cost-effective system for deaf-blind and visually impaired people. Through both outdoor and interior applications, as well as walking in even unfamiliar locations without relying on others.

articleTitle: Thermal Stress Effect on 3D Integrated Circuit Performance and Reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The technology of the through silicon vias (TSVs) plays a significant role in 3D integrated circuits (3D ICs). TSVs have the ability to vertically facilitate enormous and short interconnects between stacked silicon dies to create 3D integrated circuits; thus, increasing their value and functionality. The fabrication of TSVs undergoes several stages and can be performed in different ways. However, the mismatch of the coefficient thermal expansion (CTE) between the material of TSV and silicon substrates has resulted in the accumulation of crack driving force and tensile hoop stress in the silicon substrate. In this paper, thermal stress, its effect on the 3D IC devices, and the solutions proposed in several studies to increase performance and reliability of 3D ICs were examined.

articleTitle: Development of Unmanned Surface Vehicle with Real-time Water Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Conventionally, the water sample need to be sent to laboratory for lab analysis and take about 2-3 months. Therefore, the development and analysis of on-the-go water monitoring system using unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is proposed. The developed USV with the water monitoring system can measure and analyze the water pollution on the-go to and real time to determine the pollution level. The ISE sensor such as temperature, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), oxidation reduction potential (ORP), dissolved oxygen (DO) and turbidity with the GPS device is used on the. The USV also developed with auto navigation through all the targeted area by using GPS coordinate and path planning algorithm programmed in the USV controller. In this project, we use the IoT application to store data in the cloud and to dispense the information. The correlation of the ISE sensor and the lab analysis will be done. This system will also give out status of the water quality and immediate warning if the water is in the bad quality for further action to be taken by the management of the reservoir. Last but not least, the contribution of this research is that the use of USV helps to improve sensing and monitoring of water quality in remote area.

articleTitle: Generating Network Intrusion Image through IGTD Algorithm for CNN Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Stealthy attacks make Intrusion Detection System (IDS) research perennial and notably important. From the literature, a few problems were identified in IDS studies particularly with regards to image generation. Image generation is the preprocessing phase during the development of CNN classifier. Simple feature extraction process that are applied in a few studies may lose features’ details. They disregard spatial information such as pair pixels information. Secondly several public datasets suffer from realistic network traits. This study will apply the improvised version of IGTD algorithm to resolve image generation process. IGTD algorithm has been adopted in Cancer Cell Lines (CCLs) study. Realistic dataset of CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 and CICIDS2017 will be run over the algorithm. These dataset have been reviewed to be the closest realistic production network dataset. Result shows the generated image has notable difference between attack and benign traffic. The highest trained classification model has achieved almost 80% of accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Cluster GAN-based model for Signature Generation and Verification
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Signatures serve as a popular method of personal identity verification in various sectors such as finance and government. Signature verification systems utilize biometric samples to differentiate between authentic and falsified signatures. Although deep learning presents a promising avenue for creating such systems, the requirement of large signature datasets presents a challenge. Current datasets are restricted in size due to privacy concerns. To overcome this limitation, a model that employs cluster generative adversarial networks is proposed. This model utilizes unconditional GANs to expand the signature dataset, which in turn can be used for deep learning-based signature verification. This model can also be potentially utilized in other domains that require privacy.

articleTitle: IoT-based Monitoring of Refrigerated Vaccine Storage: A Literature Review and a Proposed Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The storage of vaccines and other sensitive materials is a critical issue, as it requires proper temperature control to maintain their efficacy. IoT technology has emerged as a promising solution for monitoring and controlling the temperature of refrigerated vaccine storage, providing real-time temperature monitoring, data analysis, and alerts for any deviations from the desired temperature range. This paper reviews the existing literature on IoT-based solutions for monitoring the storage of vaccines and other sensitive materials. The authors survey various approaches and technologies used in these solutions, including microcontrollers, temperature sensors, wireless communication modules, cloud-based databases, and machine learning algorithms. In addition, the authors present their solution, which is based on an embedded system consisting of an ESP32 microcontroller, temperature sensors, and firebase services, along with a mobile application for remote monitoring and control. The authors identify the challenges and limitations of the existing solutions and suggest future directions for research and development. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in IoT-based solutions for monitoring the storage of vaccines and other sensitive materials and is intended to inspire further research and innovation in this field.

articleTitle: A Critical Investigation into the Blockchain Technology and Its Present-Day Uses
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The IoT is a new technology that allows for the networking and communication of digital and physical things to provide novel digital services that enhance our daily lives. Though the Internet of Things (IoT) has many benefits, its centralized design raises several problems, such as a lack of redundancy, privacy concerns, transparency, and compromised data integrity. These issues are a roadblock to further advancements in IoT software. Since Bitcoin's introduction as the first and largest cryptocurrency, blockchain technology has been widely recognized as a foundation for digital money. So yet, it has to be utilized primarily to decentralize monetary or payment systems. Blockchain's distributed transaction ledger might be used to store and transmit contracts over a network. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the most recent blockchain-related applications in the academic literature. Several research papers from the canon of literature were hand-picked for inclusion in the blockchain for their potential to advance human understanding. Several observations are examined and addressed in the latter part of the work.

articleTitle: Authentication of the Electric Vehicle with the Charging Station Using AAA Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The world has become more threatened by many droughts, floods, forest fires, hurricanes and rising temperatures due to climate change. These climatic changes caused the displacement of many of the world's population and the lack of food supply. To preserve life on Earth, alternatives to current fuels must be found to reduce carbon emissions. vehicle exhaust produces a lot of carbon dioxide every year. Therefore, the best solution is to use electric vehicles to preserve the environment and reduce carbon emissions. But the main problem with the electric vehicles is the ability to provide stations to charge them with electricity inside cities and on highways. In this paper, discuss the authentication process to connect the electric vehicle to the public charger station and complete the charging process or sell the electricity stored in the vehicle's batteries to the power grid at peak times or any other vehicle. Using packet trace simulation with AAA framework to simulate the authentication process.

articleTitle: Time-Series Forecasting of Injury Cases in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: As the global population and various kinds of accidents grow, there is an increasing concern about providing high-quality healthcare. One way to improve resource management in first-care centers and pre-hospital Emergency Medical Services (EMS) is to predict the number of cases that require immediate intervention such as injuries. In this study, we aimed to forecast the annual number of injury cases per injury type which may help raise the readiness level of the Saudi Red Crescent Authority (SRCA) and pre-hospital Emergency Medical Service (EMS), which provides critical on-scene care in response to the occurrence of various emergencies. To our knowledge, this is the first work that conducts time series forecasting to predict the annual injury cases in Saudi Arabia using the publicly available annual SRCA statistics as a dataset. This study analyzes the temporal data of each injury type and shows the best-performing algorithm, features, and hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deep Learning Optimizers for Detecting Malware Using Line Search Method under Strong Wolfe Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Optimizers play a crucial role in deep learning neural networks (DL-NNs). An optimizer is an algorithm that adjusts the parameters of deep learning neural networks (DL-NNs) to improve their performance and increase their precision. An optimizer relies heavily on a learning rate, known as tweaking hyper-parameter, which states the iteration step size while heading toward the loss function minimization. In fact, the choice of learning rate is tricky, since a low value of learning rate ends in a lengthy training process that gets a cumbersome, while a high value of learning rate leads to the selection of an inadequate weight set or an unsustainable training process. This paper proposes a novel enhanced deep learning approach called Deepictor, which aims to enhance convergence performance of the deep learning (DL) throughout prior learning rates computation using line search method under strong Wolfe conditions, which have been proven for enhancing convergence performance.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Detection for Transmission Lines Connected to Photovoltaic Systems Using Inverters DC-Link Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study proposes a ground fault detection method for transmission line systems connected to inverter-based resources (IBRs), such as electronically coupled wind turbines and solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. IBRs, typically, have an initial high-frequency transient response to power system faults with limited magnitudes of short circuit current, which is different from conventional synchronous generators. IBRs' fault contribution may impact distance protection by reducing the security or dependability of the element. Distance protection may misoperate by tripping for reverse faults or not tripping for forward faults when IBRs are the main source of fault current. The proposed ground fault detection method analyses dc voltage variation in inverters' dc-link to indicate fault location during single-line-to-ground (SLG) faults. The method is designed to aid distance protection to trip forward SLG faults faster and avoid tripping for reverse faults by communicating with the inverters through low-bandwidth communication channels. The PV system and the detection method are modeled and simulated using an electromagnetic transients program.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Cross-country Differences in Open Source Software Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study explores the heterogeneity in Open Source Software (OSS) contributions across countries and identifies differences in collaboration patterns that can explain the differences in activity levels between sampled countries. We show that countries with significant user followers on GitHub exhibit a large average membership in organizations. The results also highlight the developed countries as having a higher organizations-to-developer ratio. Based on NLP analysis of the bios of developers and organizations, we observe that countries that ranked high in GitHub activity tend to ascribe to the OSS ideology and exhibit entrepreneurial spirit. Users in countries that ranked low are likely to have students, academics, or independent security specialists engaged in GitHub activity. We hope that this work is a step towards building the necessary tools to understand OSS health across countries.

articleTitle: Use Machine Learning To Predict Court First Instance in Saudi Law by Analysis the Judicial
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Predicting the type of Saudi court is helpful for illegal people to know which court is suitable for filing proceedings. However, it isn’t very easy to expect judicial courts in Saudi law because they need a data set of cases. This requires the extraction of valuable information from countless other cases and documents. Moreover, the complexity of Saudi law, coupled with a large volume of litigation, makes this problem more difficult to predict. This paper presents the predictions of the courts of the first instance in Saudi law where the user writes the text of the case to be analyzed and then predicts the type of court suitable for this case. Our methodology uses machine learning algorithms. The prototype obtained 98.36% accuracy using the xgboost algorithm, which was applied to 607 diverse judges in cases of the General Court and the Criminal Court out of five trial courts in Saudi law.

articleTitle: On Modeling of Coupled Heave-Yaw Motion of a µ-ROV
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study outlines data-driven modeling approach for identification of coupled heave-yaw motion of a compact micro remotely operated vehicle (µ-ROV). For modeling exercise, real-time tests are carried in a pool setting using on-board gyroscope and depth sensors. The data from the sensors is then pre-processed and analyzed. The experiment employs a straightforward manoeuvre that stimulates the vehicle in the vertical plane. The results indicate that yaw motion is caused by a coupling effect brought on by the reaction torque of the single vertical thruster. This enables the dynamic model to be determined in horizontal plane. A transfer function model structure is used to identify the coupled model, and it is found that the model synthesised using the suggested methodology agrees with the experimental findings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Propagation Predictions for Last-mile Connectivity in a CubeSat Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: CubeSats is seen as an innovative approach to provide many wireless communications services in a wide footprint coverage manner. However, this could lead to electromagnetic spectrum congestion, which requires larger bandwidths. Thus, optimization approaches and considering of high frequency bands are needed. This work aims to develop an optimized propagation model to enhance the last-mile connectivity of a CubeSat system using an enhanced version of the log-normal shadowing propagation model by considering elevation angle in its formulation. Then, a linear iterative feedback scheme is applied to produce an enhanced approximate solution of the propagation problem. Link budget parameters, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) have been used as performance indictors to validate the proposed scheme. Results show that the optimized model outperforms the non-optimized one from link budget and the two regression metric validation perspectives.

articleTitle: A simple low cost and highly efficient operation technique of three phase AC voltage controllers
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Three phase AC voltage controllers ACVC have many industrial and residential applications. Thyristors and TRIACS play very important role in AC voltage controller ACVC. Synchronization of control signals with supply voltages is required for proper and balanced operation of power switches in ACVC. This paper presents a novel and low-cost synchronization and control signals generation for either thyristors or TRIACS in three phase AC voltage controllers. A single comparator and a single chip microcontroller are utilized for synchronization and real time operation of the power switches achieving smooth and fast control of the output voltage. The proposed technique avoids the problems of complex circuitries required in conventional operation of those power switches. Simulation and experimental validation of the proposed technique are presented. The three phase ACVC based on the proposed technique is applied as a soft starter of three phase induction motor.

articleTitle: Malware Detection Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In this article, we delve into the realm of malware detection, We’ve created an advanced deep learning method designed to classify malicious software contained in an executable files. This stands in sharp contrast to traditional malware detection systems that depend on signatures, our method hinges on static detection techniques for discerning between malicious and benign files. We introduce an efficient deep learning technique for the identification of malware. Our proposed method leverages a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN) specifically tailored to the characteristics of portable executable files. Empirically, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing it to state-of-the-art methods across three datasets. The experimental results unequivocally show that our approach surpasses several classification models, providing a practical, dependable, and swift means of detecting malware in executable files.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Usage Evaluation Strategy for Mobile E-Learning Systems in KSA Institutions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Saudi Arabia has more than 50 public and private universities. There are around 30,000 elementary and secondary schools. Students receive free education, textbooks, and medical care, and everyone can enroll. Effective mobile e-learning apps improve learning, cognition, and memory. No method or theory assesses or accesses user perception and usability features. This inquiry combined quantitative and qualitative methods. Students' mobile app demands and thoughts are surveyed using quantitative analysis. Considering the user's (student's) perspective, we ranked usability based on efficiency. Before determining a final rating, each usability factor was considered. KNN predicts usability based on the Machine Learning Model with 99.8% accuracy. This method evaluates e-learning programmes' usability demands.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design of Wireless Smart Grid for the Optimization of Electric Transmission in Iraq
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Rapid development of technology has resulted in a considerable increase in electricity consumption, which has created a barrier not only because of the generation but also in delivery. Thus, when demand increases, the complexity of the electrical network increases as a result of the increased need for improved dependability, efficiency, protection, energy, and environmental sustainability. According to the world bank statistics, Iraq's loss was 51% during distribution, and it is considered significantly high. This study proposes a wireless network-based design for detecting and optimizing Iraq's electricity distribution infrastructure. Moreover, the suggested module is composed of several data gathering methods that are required for the various paths of the power distribution systems. This design offers viable support for a variety of issues confronting Iraq's power distribution systems, including variable voltage levels caused by fluctuating electrical usage, power burglary, manual invoicing, and transmission line breakdowns. The suggested design is intended for use with single-phase power transmission systems; however, it may be adapted for use with three-phase power distribution systems with slight improvements. The introduction of this method will result in significant energy savings, allowing for the availability of electricity to a greater number of users than previously possible in a crowded place. The suggested smart grid design, which was created for the Iraq context, permits real-time control of energy consumption, optimal electricity consumption, minimal loss, diagnosis of power failures, breakdowns, and automatic invoicing.

articleTitle: Work in Progress: The Effectiveness of Knowledge Management System on Companies Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the current challenging environment with the highly speed development that the companies’ world faced, finding and keeping up with the auxiliary tools and systems has become a requirement and a necessity to deal with the complexity and uncertainty changes. One of the efficient ways to reach the previous goal is to implement knowledge management system (KMS). KMS is a systematic way that stores and retrieves knowledge to improve the process of understanding and collaboration [1]. The major purpose of this research is to examine the effectiveness of the knowledge management system on performance and a case study of Petroleum Development Oman (PDO) company is selected. This research will adopt mixed methodology consisting of quantitative and qualitative approaches through conducting questionnaire and interviews primarily. In addition to evaluate literature review as additional source. After that, the collected data will be analyzed with the appropriate data analysis technique.

articleTitle: Predictive modeling of the rate-distortion of scalable video sequences based on complexity
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Rate-Distortion (R-D) models are applied in video processing techniques to predict the bit rate required for the transmission of video sequences in the networks. Video coding techniques are utilized to smartly divide the bandwidth in the communication networks. This research presents predictive modeling of the Rate-Distortion of scalable video sequences based on complexity. Base-Layer (BL) rate and Enhancement-Layer (EL) rate models are developed alongside R-D models to get more precise rate predictions. Videos will be classified based on low and high complexity. This classification is achieved by the Spatial-Index (SI) and Temporal-Index (TI) of video sequences Group of Pictures (GOP) wise. By using the role of SI and TI, an algorithm is developed to predict the rate required by video sequences of low and high complexity with the given distortion and vice versa. The experimental results have shown the productive comparison of presented R-D models and existing R-D models.

articleTitle: A Unified Framework for Multi-Language Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The unified framework for multi-language sentiment analysis is a vital aspect of understanding customer opinions, emotions, and feedback. This paper presents a unified framework to increase the performance of the multi-language sentimental analysis. Two popular machine translation services, Google Translate, and Yandex Translate are employed to unify the sentiment analysis for the considered languages including English, Turkish, Arabic, and French. Our findings highlight the importance of machine translation services in facilitating and enhancing the performance of sentiment analysis algorithms for different languages. Our framework was evaluated on several datasets and showed promising results, with improvements in accuracy ranging from 1% to 22% depending on the language. Our approach outperforms language-specific models and demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed translation-based multi-language framework. In addition, we found that the performance of sentiment analysis varies among the different languages, with Google Translate exhibiting better performance in sentiment analysis of Turkish and Arabic translations while Yandex Translate shows better results in sentiment analysis of English and French translations.

articleTitle: Control of Steady-State Disturbances in Microgrids using Smell Agent Symbiotic Organism Search
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an optimal control of steady-state disturbances in the power flow of microgrids. In microgrid operations, the variation in loads induces instability in line-parameters such as voltage and frequency, resulting in a decrease in power quality and overall system stability. To address these challenges, a Smell Agent Symbiotic Organism Search (SASOS) algorithm, which integrates Smell Agent Optimizer (SAO) and Symbiosis Organism Search (SOS) algorithms, was codified in the design of an optimized controller to improve power quality control. The SASOS, SAO, and SOS algorithms were applied in the Microgrid’s Centralized Controller (MCC) for the control of steady-state disturbances. The simulation results showed the viability of the MCC-SASOS technique compared to the MCC-SOS, MCC-SAO, and MCC techniques.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm For Convolutional Neural Network Hyperparameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Image classification has been applied in various fields, from agriculture to health. In order to perform well, an image classification method needs an appropriate hyperparameter setting. However, tuning hyperparameters in a classification method is not an easy task. Many approaches have been developed to solve the problem, such as combining metaheuristics methods with a convolutional neural network (CNN). An example of metaheuristics method is genetic algorithm. Genetic algorithms have been proven to optimize machine learning and deep learning. This research contributes to the automatic tuning of hyperparameters using genetic algorithms. The proposed method is evaluated using MNIST dataset. The experiments results show that using a genetic algorithm for tuning hyperparameters automatically, the accuracy of validation data is 97.02% and the accuracy of training data is 99.77%. The performance of Genetic Algorithm is compared with Harmony Search. The accuracy of Harmony Search for validation data is 83.96% and for training data is 88.33%. The Genetic algorithm takes 24,97 seconds for training while Harmony Search needs 56.44 seconds.

articleTitle: Neural Network Algorithm for a Gravity-Driven Fluid Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This article aims to find out the enhancement in the heat transfer rate. A mathematical model for the nanofluids flow over a starched surface is considered. The flow of the fluid is due to the convection force which is happening due to the vertical sheet. The artificial neural networking (ANN) strategy is used to solve a mathematical model for the hybrid nanofluids flow on an extending sheet. The sheet is extending and kept vertical, where the flow is due to the gravity force in the downward direction. The basic equations of the flow field are transformed from PDEs to ODEs using the proper transformations. To assess the performance of LMS-NNA (Least Mean Square Neural Network Algorithm), various statistical neural network tools are employed, such as mean square error, regression plots, curve fitting graphs, and error histograms

articleTitle: High Gain and Efficiency Triple U-shaped Slots Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The 28 GHz band is a frequency band that has been allocated for use in 5G mobile communication networks. It is part of the millimeter wave spectrum, which is a range of frequencies between 30 GHz and 300 GHz. This study proposes and investigates the 28 GHz 5G networks. A modified single element patch antenna with three grooved U-shaped holes is shown and is used to indicate a high gain and Efficiency for 28 GHz 5G antenna. The proposed antenna consists of the radiation element on a RTRogers 5880 laminate and is actuated by a microstrip feedline. The proposed work includes the most desirable characteristics, such as small size, light weight, low-cost fabrication and wide operation up to 1.4 GHz (27.1 - 28.5 GHz). The proposed antenna design also offers a high efficiency up to 89.73 %, high gain up to 8.14 dBi, and return loss up to −30 dB, resulting in attractive performance. The results obtained show that the antenna is a viable candidate for 5G applications at 28 GHz.

Author Keywords: Triple U-shaped slot High Gain and Efficiency

articleTitle: Towards an Ontology-Based E-Learning Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: E-learning recommendation systems enhance learning for students (e-learners) through their provision of tailored recommendations to student queries. Existing e-learning recommendation systems have relied on traditional algorithms, such as collaborative filtering, which are limited when tasked to provide recommendations for new users. This paper contributes to the body of work on personalised recommendation systems by proposing a multi-task ontology based framework capable of supporting multiple personalised recommendations for multiple purposes. These may include personalised learning paths, objects (such as courses or textbooks) and feedback. To generate personalised feedback, the approach uses a rule based system that integrates ontological information to learner profiles in order to provide a recommendation. Additionally, the framework provisions for domain-expert generated feedback to e-learners.

articleTitle: Expand Object Detection Dataset Automatically via Deep Learning Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Object detection is an important research field in image processing. The state-of-the-art machine learning models are trained with huge number of samples to solve this problem. Manually labeling objects on images is labor intensive, expensive, and time consuming. It is desirable to create an automatic labeling system to reduce the cost and the time needed. A deep learning neural networks based automatic labeling system is proposed in this paper to expand Microsoft Common Objects in Context 2017 (COCO 2017) dataset from 80 classes to 81 classes by adding labels for the new class, human faces, automatically. The system contains an Auto-Labeling Model (ALM) which is trained using Web Image Dataset for Event Recognition FACE (WIDER FACE) dataset. ALM detects faces in COCO 2017 dataset and provides bounding boxes automatically with very high accuracy. The generated new labels by ALM are merged to the existing labels in COCO 2017 dataset automatically. 4,110 hours human effort is saved using this system. The expanded COCO 2017 dataset is evaluated quantitatively and visually to ensure the efficiency of the proposed auto-labeling system.

articleTitle: Parkinson’s Disease Identification By Voice and Handwritten Drawings using Xgboost and Random Forest Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurological movement illness that starts with a subtle tremor over hand and a feel of stiffness across the body. It affects over than 6 million people worldwide. Particularly in the beginning stages of the disease when symptom identification is extremely hard, there is currently no specific diagnosis for this condition by non- specialist doctors. This technique uses spiral design and speech to identify Parkinson's disease. The voice wobbles will confirm the characteristics of Parkinson's illness. The efficiency of eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Random Forest Algorithms would be higher than 73.8%. For this model, the considerable amount of data is gathered from both healthy people and people who have already faced with Parkinson's disease. These are trained using machine learning algorithms includes XGBoost, Random Forest.
