The voice data set consists of 24 columns, all but the status column of which will display a patient's symptom values. There are 0s and 1s in the status column. The factors include spectral moments: mean, standard deviation, skewness determines whether a person has Parkinson's disease from the voice data set. 1s indicate an impacted person, while 0s imply healthy person. The analysis of Handwritten drawings will indicate the condition of the patient’s health whether affected by Parkinson’s disease or not. The prediction of the handwritten drawings will be either healthy or impacted person.

articleTitle: Decentralized Framework for Cultural Heritage Conservation using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The preservation and management of cultural heritage sites and artifacts is an important task that requires efficient and secure methods for data management and access control. Blockchain technology, with its decentralized architecture and immutability features, has the potential to provide innovative solutions for these challenges. This research aims to explore the use of blockchain technology for the preservation and management of cultural heritage sites and artifacts. The study will focus on the design and implementation of a decentralized framework that allows for the collaborative conservation and restoration of cultural heritage, using blockchain-based smart contracts and digital tokens. The framework will also provide secure and transparent access control mechanisms for the management and sharing of cultural heritage data among stakeholders, including researchers, conservationists, and the general public. The research will also evaluate the potential benefits and limitations of the proposed framework and its impact on the preservation and management of cultural heritage.

articleTitle: A Formal Approach to Component Adaptation with a Tool Support
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In a component-based software development, the only way to describe components is through interfaces since they are considered as black boxes. Indeed, their interfaces (required and provided) allow to express their visible behaviors. The connection between interfaces must be ensured in a suitable manner. The connection of two incompatible interfaces requires the use of a software adaptor. In this work, we define notions of compatibility between a required and a provided interfaces by focusing on protocol level. Then we specify adaptor in case of incompatibles intefaces. Finally, we check that compatibility by using the B formal method, based on the concept of refinement, and having powerful tool support, the B prover.

articleTitle: The Impact of Remote Work on Corporate Security
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The increased use of remote working in the corporate world has led to an escalation of cybersecurity threats to corporate networks. Numerous studies have explored the impact of remote work on corporate security, including potential threats and recommended best practices. However, there is a significant research gap in these areas, highlighting the need for more studies to compare key findings and identify the most effective best practices. To address these gaps, the present study systematically analyzes recent research on the impacts of remote working on corporate security. A total of 10 empirical studies were identified based on specific criteria, including the publication date and relevance to the study focus. The research findings shed light on the impact of remote working on corporate security and highlight potentials risks and best practices. These practices include never storing passwords in plain text, regularly changing passwords, using passwords with a minimum length of eight characters, selecting memorable passwords, promptly reporting data compromise or password loss, and reporting violations of company guidelines. Companies can implement these best practices to enhance corporate security. Workforces and information security managers should prioritize efforts to mitigate threats associated with remote working.

articleTitle: A High Quality Secure Medical Image Steganography Method
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The exchange of medical images over the Internet has prompted substantial claims on the last years due to the presentation of cloud-based medical data systems according to various web services in the area of telemedicine applications. The preservation of confidential information has ever been a key indicator of the effectiveness of these systems. In this paper, an efficient data hiding technique is proposed for Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) images hence security can be specified for the highly invaluable and private sensitive data of the patient. The proposed method is developed for DICOM images to embed Patient Record Information (PRI) for maintaining the fidelity of both the critical components of the image and private patient data. The proposed method is very effective in telemedicine applications as it can increase the security of the PRI during its transmission over the Internet from different remote places.

articleTitle: Intelligent Eczema management and awareness system for Saudi Arabia System Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Eczema disease diagnosis and treatment are frequently challenging procedures. Recent development in artificial intelligence (AI) or digital healthcare technology have improved the self-management of severe chronic diseases. for example, skin conditions, insulin, pressure, etc. Numerous research has validated its effectiveness. Additionally, studies have also shown that greater knowledge about any illness enables people to properly control their chronic health conditions, which in turn lowers the problems brought on by disorders such as diabetes, eczema, and hypertension. In this research, a novel dermatitis illness monitoring and treatment system is presented for Saudi Arabian patients. The technology being shown uses AI in conjunction with smart healthcare technology. Employing digital healthcare technologies and AI, it also hopes to arm eczema patients with numerous features about the condition. Comprehensive testing and evaluation of the method that this research proposes will take place in a randomized scientific experiment in Saudi Arabic.

articleTitle: Action Localization and Recognition through Unsupervised I3D and TSN
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Since CCTV technology was widely introduced as a video surveillance system, it has become very popular due to increased security concerns. However, detecting suspicious behavior is still done manually by humans, which is inefficient in terms of accuracy and manpower (prone to distraction and fatigue). Many studies use the entire frame of a video to recognize human action, whereas in this study first localize the area of object movement using the unsupervised inflated 3D (I3D) network which produces several frames that have been determined as the region of interest (ROI) from the total frames in the video. Then the collection of ROI frames is generated into a video which will then be classified to recognize human action through the Temporal Segment Networks (TSN). For efficiency purposes, the proposed pipeline can be run separately in the edge (for localization), and cloud environment (for recognition), respectively. The results show that there are 54 classes of ROI video data sets that have an average human action recognition prediction similarity rate above 84.6% which is the average of the prediction similarity rate of the entire ROI video data. In terms of prediction accuracy, 37 classes of data (36.63%) are better than the original class, including 25 classes of data (24.75%) above the threshold, and the processing speed of classification with ROI video data is on average 5 times faster than full-frame video data.

articleTitle: Mango Farming Optimization With AI: Boosting Cultivation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Mangoes have long played an important role in global import and export, but a fall in mango commerce has been seen over the past few years, preventing producers from meeting market demand. The predominant cause of this loss is the prevalence of mango tree disease, which finally transforms healthy and fruitful mango orchids into low-yield varieties. Our proposed approach offers a "Mango Leaf Health Detection Dataset" for mango tree health detection. The dataset has been validated and tested with YOLO v5s, YOLO v7, and YOLO v8s. The YOLO Algorithm analyzes the image of the leaf by passing it through a pipeline consisting of redefining the image in grid cells, constructing bounding boxes, and predicting the class. This not only saves time, but also delivers accurate and effective results, thereby designating the area of the orchid where pesticide must be treated. Our trained YOLO v7 detection video can be found ${\color{Blue}\text{here}}$, and the dataset used can be accessed ${\color{Blue}\text{here}}$.

articleTitle: A Moving-Horizon Estimator of the Unmeasured States for Fuel Sloshing Dynamics in Close Proximity Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Understanding how measurement noise influences sloshing dynamics is required to comprehend how it affects space vehicles in proximity operations. Despite researchers’ interest in space vehicle dynamics in proximity operations, few studies have explored the implications of measurement noise on its dynamics. However, one key problem encountered is poor estimation of the system state variable, which leads to poor control of the system. As a result, this study attempts to solve this issue by offering a scheme for providing critical information on the optimal estimation of the unmeasured states of the fuel sloshing dynamics. The approach was primarily based on moving horizon estimator-based model predictive control. The results obtained demonstrated the efficiency of the moving-horizon estimator in estimating unmeasured state variables. Hence, when the effects of measurement noise are considered, the moving horizon estimator provides a good assessment of the unmeasured states in a proximity operation.

articleTitle: Combining CNNs and Bi-LSTMs for Enhanced Network Intrusion Detection: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems have become more popular as cloud technologies have become more widely adopted. This paper presents a network intrusion detection system using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) models. The NSL-KDD dataset is being used in the current study for analyzing the efficiency of the model. The data is pre-processed to handle missing values and normalize the features, and a stratified K-Fold cross-validation is used for analyzing the efficiency of the model. The results show that the combination of CNNs and Bi-LSTMs can effectively detect network intrusions and outperforms traditional intrusion detection methods. This study provides a new approach to network intrusion detection and highlights the potential of deep learning models in this field. The proposed system demonstrated exceptional performance with a high accuracy of 99.308% and a low false positive rate of below 0.23%, effectively indicating its capability to detect network intrusions while generating minimal false alarms.

articleTitle: Effects of Face Image Degradation on Recognition with Vision Transformers: Review and Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Vision Transformers have been recently introduced and achieved great success in the last two years beating convolutional neural networks (CNN) in many computer vision applications including Face Transformer for face recognition. However, one of the rising concerns is how sensitive these models are to various types of image degradations, especially when used for biometric authentication and person identification. This research aims at reviewing related work and presenting a case study to investigate the robustness of a fine-tuned version of Face Transformer under different pose, age, and gender variations for several degradations such as noise, blur, and resolution reduction. Several experiments have been conducted to train and test the model using two benchmark datasets (VGGFace2 and LFW) and benchmark its performance with FaceNet.

articleTitle: Real-time Detection of Birds for Farm Surveillance Using YOLOv7 and SAHI
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: There are various causes of crop damage, and a flock of birds serves a major proportion of it. The conventional manual scaring techniques have proven to be inefficient. But the main problem is early detection of birds in the sky, where the acoustic methods prove to be less accurate. Here, the computer vision techniques come to the picture. In this study we train YOLOv7 (You Only Look Once) models and use it in co-ordination with SAHI (Slicing Aided Hyper Inference). We detect a flock of birds by counting the number of bounding boxes of birds detected in a frame of the live video feed captured through cameras, if that number is found to be greater than the decided threshold, an alarm/actuator is turned on to scare away the birds. We train two models, one for RGB videos for day-time monitoring and one for infrared videos for night-time monitoring. Finally, to test our model for accuracy and real-time performance we compute the f1 score, precision, recall and average frames per second. These types of models can be used for farm surveillance, wild animals’ detection, wind farm monitoring, endangered species counting and monitoring the vicinities of an aircraft. We observed that in case of IR Model the number of detections increased by 82% and in case of RGB Model the number of detections increased by 136.6% when SAHI was used on top of YOLOv7.

articleTitle: Automated Phrasal Verb and Key-Phrase Checking with LSTM-Based Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Text prediction and classification are crucial tasks in modern Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. Long short-term memory (LSTM), a type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), is well-known for its outstanding performance in text classification. Phrasal verbs, also known as Bagdhara in Bangla, play a vital role in making language more expressive and poetic in any language, including Bangla. These two or three-word phrases help us convey our emotions and thoughts more effectively. However, determining whether a phrase is a phrasal verb and appropriate for a given context can be challenging for writers, poets, and the general public. To address this issue, an automatic system capable of identifying and using phrasal verbs is necessary. In this study, we propose a system that can instantly and accurately predict phrasal verbs using the LSTM algorithm, a part of the RNN, and an attention mechanism. Our system achieved an overall phrasal verb prediction accuracy of 78.63%.

articleTitle: Building a Better Future Workforce: Digital Dexterity and Psychological Empowerment
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: As the business landscape progresses, the advancement of information systems is becoming increasingly valuable in shaping the future workforce. The rising demand for skilled employees who can navigate and manage technological tools and stay engaged in the workplace requires businesses to make significant efforts to advance their workforce's digital competencies and cognitive satisfaction. To understand this phenomenon better, considering the future workforce, specifically final-year students, could provide more valuable insights, as previous studies have been unable to capture this illustration fully. This research intends to understand willingness to engage behaviour of the future workforce through digital dexterity (i.e., personal-innovativeness, and computers self-efficacy) and psychological empowerment. A hypothesis-based framework delineated with seven paths, and data were collected through a questionnaire survey. To analyze the collected data from 147 respondents, a multivariate data analysis technique "PLS-SEM" was practiced. The study finding illustrated that personal innovativeness played a major role in impacting willingness to engage behavior followed by computer self-efficacy. These findings are novel and significant, providing new insights into the complex relationship between model variables among final-year students. The implications of this study would be particularly valuable for businesses looking to understand better and engage with the future workforce.

articleTitle: A Deep Hybrid Learning Approach For Nail Diseases Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In medical domains, the appearance of fingernails can provide clues to underlying systemic diseases or nutritional imbalance; the neglection of such clues could lead to unwanted health complications and less chance for recovery. In this paper, a Deep Hybrid Learning (DHL) approach was proposed to detect nail-based diseases, where a Deep Learning (DL) model is used for feature extraction, and a traditional Machine Learning (ML) classifier is used for classification. The aim is to classify three nail diseases: melanoma, beau's nails, and eczema, in addition to healthy nails. Further, the proposed approach is compared to the transfer learning approach, where a pre-trained model is used for feature extraction and classification. The experiment results indicate that the DHL approach is superior to the transfer learning approach. Specifically, the architecture where the DenseNet201 pre-trained model is used for feature extraction and the SGDClassifier is used for classification, as it achieved an accuracy of 94%.

articleTitle: Analysis and Forecasting of Saudi Stock Market Using Time Series Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Forecasting the stock market is essential for investors to help assess the potential financial movement of the market value. Therefore, accurate estimation of the movement and price of the stock contributes more to the profit of investors through making informed investment judgments. Thus, the popularity of forecasting the stock market increased because of the difficulty of this field and that it is unforecastable and cannot be controlled because of its volatile nature and is affected by several factors. Nevertheless, the field of machine learning succeeded in forecasting the future stock market based on the analysis of time series data collected over time. The main objective of this paper is to develop day-to-day forecast models in ways that have been popular among researchers through time series data collected from the Saudi stock market, Tadawul, containing daily observations of the Tadawul All Share Index (TASI), and a different sample of some companies listed under the TASI. In our analysis, we relied on the technical approach, so it was important to choose technical indicators most closely related to the closing price of the next day using feature engineering and feature selection. Then, this study conducted two different models of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) time series techniques. Best expected results Performance was evaluated using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) scale. The results show that LSTM algorithms based on deep learning are better than the ARIMA statistical model in stock market forecasting.

articleTitle: An Online Randomized Field Experiment on the Importance of Privacy Education, Training, and Awareness (PETA)
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study examines the effect of privacy awareness on decisions to disclose personal information related to various security measures at the individual level. Explaining and predicting why individuals decide to disclose or withhold security-related preferences and behaviors (e.g., use of password, passphrase, 2-factor authentication, frequency of updating security software and operating systems, etc.) is a critical research and practice endeavor because such personal information is highly sensitive and can be detrimental when it lands in the hands of social engineers. We conducted a randomized field experiment in which privacy awareness was manipulated via a simple privacy nudge and disclosure behavior was measured by asking subjects to respond to a series of personal questions related to security preferences and behaviors. The experiment was conducted online among Saudi Arabian subjects who signed up for a 2-hour Security Education, Training, and Awareness (SETA) workshop during which they learned about various security protection measures. We used a basic between-subjects experimental design and conducted the experiment in three waves of data collection (N = 2,668): wave 1 was conducted immediately prior to the SETA workshop; wave 2 was conducted immediately after the SETA workshop; and wave 3 was conducted two weeks after the SETA workshop. Our aim is to test whether the privacy awareness nudge makes a difference in terms of whether individuals disclose information related to their security preferences and behaviors. The findings show that our participants overall disclosed most information asked for in waves 1, 2, and 3. This is an alarming observation regardless of the context of our experiment. However, participants who received the privacy nudge disclosed less information than those who did not receive the privacy nudge in waves 1, 2, and 3. These findings suggest that Privacy Education, Training, and Awareness (PETA) is necessary to supplement existing SETA programs. We discuss our contribution to the cybersecurity literature and practice and provide a short conclusion on how our experiment applies to what we coin the ‘general relativity of privacy’.

articleTitle: Detect Alzheimer’s Disease from Neuroimaging Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the continuous deterioration of cognitive, behavioral, and social skills that affects a person’s ability to function independently. It is the most common cause of memory impairment and dementia. Early detection is considered one of the most important factors that helps make plans and prevent the development of symptoms of this disease. The purpose of this work is to compare machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models to detect early warning signs of AD. In addition, a neural network is utilized to extract important features and distinguish between healthy brain imaging and that of those affected by mild cognitive impairment (MCI). A 3D convolutional neural network (3D-CNN) architecture is utilized to compute the features of neuroimaging data. After that, the feature vector is fed to the support vector machines (SVM) for final recognition. The system is assessed using a publicly available ADNI dataset for functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). In the case of a 3D convolutional neural network, a recognition rate of 98.92% and 98.3% is attained on training and testing, respectively. In the case of the SVM model, an accuracy of 97.14% and 97.5% is achieved on training and testing, respectively.

articleTitle: Authentication Schemes for Internet of Drones: Taxonomy, Threat Models, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) has lately acquired popularity because to its flexibility to a broad variety of difficult situations. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) can be utilised efficiently in surveillance, agriculture, search-and-rescue operations, and mission-critical services. Drones have a lot of technological and practical benefits, including high mobility, the potential to increase cellular coverage regions, and the capacity to explore difficult sites. Since the majority of applications employing drones in the IoD are real-time based, Users want instantaneous access to the services provided by the deployed drones operating within a specified flight area. To solve this major problem in the IoD, we need a efficient and secure user authentication protocol that would allow an authorized user, such an ambulance driver, to have immediate access to data from a nearby drone. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of authentication schemes for IoD communication. We discuss the applications in IoD, vulnerabilities, attacks, and challenges, with a focus on the existing authentication protocols, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of the various techniques. This paper also explores the area of authentication and the possibility for developing lightweight and new IoD authentication protocols.

articleTitle: Microscopic Bacterial Classification Using Deep Learning Based on Augmented Reality Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Based on colony morphology, scientists have classified the bacterial colony by visual screening. This process requires trained scientists as beginners may make mistakes identifying bacterial types. Artificial intelligence advancement, along with augmented reality, offer an opportunity to automate the classification process without human interactions. Deep learning has been widely implemented in microbiology. This research proposed a newly collected dataset of bacterial microscopic images containing 1,140 images of three different bacterial strains. This dataset has been utilized by VGG-16 and ResNet-50 for classification purposes. The results achieved 99.4% accuracy in both models. This research also proposed an architecture of Mobile Augmented Reality (MAR) to train deep learning models on more images using mobile devices. Performance may be improved further with more images of bacterial colonies.

articleTitle: Real-time Plant Disease Segmentation and Identification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Farmers usually face the common issue of plant pests and diseases that affect their crop productivity and yield. Misdiagnosis and mistreatment of the crop's condition will lead to a similar outcome further amplifying the harm of the problem. To take the guesswork out of farming and provide an immediate and convenient plant disease advisory, we propose a real-time plant disease segmentation and identification approach using transfer learning that accurately detects local plant diseases affecting crops and offers a corresponding step-by-step treatment measure. A real dataset of local plant diseases was used to train several CNN architectures such as EfficientNet, ResNet and VGG. Prior to the training stage, advanced preprocessing and segmentation techniques were used to enhance the images and efficiently extract the region of interest, which further enable transfer learning more effectively. The best-performing model when the accuracy and prediction time efficiency combined are considered is the EfficientNet-B0 model, resulted in a prediction time of 0.0145 seconds, an overall accuracy of 99.0%, and a mean F1 score of 98.7%. Moreover, we integrated the best-performing model into a mobile application (named PlantDoc) for further validation and usage in a real-world scenario.

articleTitle: A Review of Blockchain Use Cases and Recent Failures in the Enterprise
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has facilitated decentralized digital transformation by enabling peer-to-peer transactions and eliminating intermediaries. It blends a set of useful properties, such as decentralization, transparency, immutability, and traceability, making it applicable to various use cases. However, the number of enterprise blockchain solutions reaching production stages is limited. Additionally, challenges and failures have extended to the use of blockchain to manage supply chains, which is one of the most promising applications of blockchain. This paper reviews blockchain opportunities, use cases, and challenges in the enterprise. It examines the recent setbacks of blockchain-based supply chain projects and discusses factors that may have impacted their progress. Considering these factors should help to avoid similar future project failures. Consequently, we recommend extending the current blockchain’s decision frameworks to cover and mitigate them. Moreover, we propose a high-level risk management process that is inspired by the practices of implementing large-scale enterprise projects. Blockchain projects should learn from and apply these project management practices and frameworks that have a large body of knowledge accumulated for decades.

articleTitle: Data Mining and Visualization to Understand Employee Attrition and Work Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Throughout the course of careers, a large number of employees encounter a variety of normal life events that can have an impact on their performance and job environment satisfaction. Under these circumstances, some employees are compelled to leave their positions, not because of issues with their work environment, but due to personal circumstances. This is what we refer to as Employee Attrition, a pervasive phenomenon affecting numerous businesses and work environments in the present day. Employee attrition could occur in a variety of ways and be determined by several entities. Therefore, we look into various conditions, causes, indicators, and entities in order to study the attrition problem and determine its answers and enhancements. This study investigated the attrition of employees based on IBM data repository, together with the machine learning based experimental analysis and knowledge discoveries, to identify the most effective approaches to the attrition problem. The experimental data contained 1,471 records with 35 distinct characteristics. We formally employed Nave Bayes Classifier in this study using WEKA datamining software, and adequate knowledge has been extracted to better comprehend employee turnover and their work performance facets.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing to Detect Fake News in Arabic: A Survey Paper
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Due to recent progress in the World Wide Web and the expansion of social networking platforms, the dissemination of counterfeit information has gained momentum, leading to the proliferation of misinformation and misguided convictions among individuals and society in general. To address this escalating concern, artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques are being employed to construct automated detection models. Deep learning (DL) models exhibit substantial potential in managing intricate tasks related to natural language processing, thereby constituting a valuable tool in the context of detecting counterfeit news. Our objective is to formulate an Adam optimization-driven deep learning approach, termed the ADL-FNDC model, with the purpose of proficiently distinguishing fabricated news from genuine news sources. The ADL-FNDC model underwent preprocessing and word embedding using the GloVe algorithm. We then employed a deep belief network approach to detect and classify fake news.

articleTitle: Maize Plant Disease Prediction of UAV Images for Precision Agriculture Using Fusion of Multimodal
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The agriculture sector is vital to a country’s economic and productive development. With technological advancements, we can identify plant diseases in their early stages, similar to how human diseases are diagnosed, and avoid significant financial loss. For example, a new technique has been developed to detect diseases in maize crops, a widely used raw product in the food industry and precision agriculture. Furthermore, farmers ensure the fields do not remain wet for extended periods to prevent fungus infection. Currently, machine learning and deep learning approaches are being utilized, making agriculture one of the most researched topics in AI. This study proposes a novel framework for predicting maize plant disease using a fusion of multi-deep learning models. The proposed framework uses a four-stage pipeline for detecting disease in maize plants by fusion of Xception, DenseNet-121, and ensembling of Xception and DenseNet-121 models to achieve excellent results on the OSF drone image dataset, which consists of 1821 high-resolution images of maize plants taken from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The accuracy of our proposed approach is 96.95%, which is highly effective, considering the challenges posed by drone images.

articleTitle: Multi-Attribute Featured Layout Generation forGraphic Design using Capsule Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Graphic design is a very individualized and variable undertaking for which it is challenging to find a single answer. Layout modeling is an essential initial stage in graphic design. The generation of visual layouts has improved recently, especially with the development of generative adversarial networks (GANs). The issue of defining the positions and dimensions of design components, however, often includes restrictions with regard to element properties, such as size, aspect ratio, and reading-order. This concept of "inverse graphics," which is the opposite of how computers (often) generate pictures, is one that Caps Net seeks to adopt. The network here begins with a picture and attempts to identify the items it includes as well as its instantiation properties, including posture (size, orientation, and relative position). When creating a typographic piece that combines text and an image, designers first place the design elements over the proper area before adjusting the size and location of the original component arrangement to get the best visual result. Position, dimension, and scale factors are used to alter different design components for this. For cutting-edge engineering applications like virtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR), image reconstructions, contemporary sports analytics, target tracking, pose-based video games, driving assistance, and posture estimation is a crucial job. In this study, we use a multi-GPU infrastructure to build Capsule Networks to tackle the pose estimation problem for rigid object computer graphics. The necessity for reciprocal interactions among the intended components distinguishes layout creation from pixel-level picture synthesis. Experiments in both the quantitative and qualitative realms show how visually comparable the produced layouts are to actual design layouts. For a deeper knowledge of the aesthetic quality, we can create actual designs based on expected layouts. Finally, we provide a real-world example of layout suggestion.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation: Deep Learning-based Intelligent Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Currently, chatbots face the issues such as inadequate use of multi-modality information, poor feelings of expression competence, and a lack of a model fusion mechanism. Deep learning applications include NLP-based "natural language understanding (NLU)", sentiment analysis, machine translation, and word vector representation. People have started looking into the new capabilities of chatbots and applying deep learning techniques to chatbots. Provided the actual problem that conventional chatbots Seq-2-Seq model training tends to produce quite secure, widely accepted, and repetitive responses to the speech corpus, this article utilizes the understanding of cooperative pieces of evidence to develop the optimization problem of the model in order to generate better and much more versatile response by the model and can provide to the client with a better and expected and quality outcome. Results of the experiment revealed that the model was found to outperform the single model in many indicators in the short text given data experiment.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Privacy Via Differential Privacy Of Smart Metering Data
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The information collected by smart meters may be used in several ways. The collection and analysis of this data needed a substantial amount of time and money for the development of the smart grid. Despite the potential advantages of smart meters, the dissemination of such data could have a considerable effect on the lack of privacy. Implementing algorithms for power analysis to gather and disclose a user’s personal information and interests based on the amount of power the user consumes has shown this. To protect the privacy of customers, we recommend using a differential privacy model for data aggregation after the collection of data by smart meters. To demonstrate this, we have used the Laplace mechanism to the row records of the smart meters, which protects the confidentiality of customer information.

articleTitle: Combining data mining with rigorous whole-genome phylogenetics enables detailed comparative genomics from over 2.3 million genomes across Coronaviridae
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Coronavirus outbreaks continue to pose significant public health challenges worldwide. Investigating the emergence of coronaviruses such as Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is crucial to form a nuanced understanding of outbreaks past and present, as well as plan for potential future risks. Furthermore, as new variants continue to emerge, understanding the historical and evolutionary context of coronaviruses across the various clades within Coronaviridae can better inform potential recombination hotspots from regions of local homology across clades. This work is distinct in adopting a novel, computationally demanding, data-driven, bottom-up approach to consider the entire genomic landscape of all deposited coronaviruses at the time of writing in a single comparative framework, enabling a more comprehensive, integrative genomic understanding and contextualization of known coronaviruses. We demonstrate a general methodological approach applicable throughout evolutionary and comparative genomics, whereby we exhaustively clustered 2.32 million genomes, computationally selected thousands of strain-level representative genomes spanning the entirety of known coronaviruses, and performed rigorous multiple-sequence-alignment and phylogenetic inference and bootstrapping techniques typically considered feasible only for small-scale problems, and further probed the evolutionary relationship and regions of homology between MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 within context of Coronaviridae as a whole.

articleTitle: SIFT – File Fragment Classification Without Metadata
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: A vital issue of file carving in digital forensics is type classification of file fragments when the filesystem metadata is missing. Over the past decades, there have been several efforts for developing methods to classify file fragments. In this research, a novel sifting approach, named SIFT (Sifting File Types), is proposed. SIFT outperforms the other state-of-the-art techniques by at least 8%. (1) One of the significant differences between SIFT and others is that SIFT uses a single byte as a separate feature, i.e., a total of 256 (0×00 – 0×FF) features. We also call this a lossless feature (information) extraction, i.e., there is no loss of information. (2) The other significant difference is the technique used to estimate inter-Classes and intra-Classes information gain of a feature. Unlike others, SIFT adapts TF-IDF for this purpose, and computes and assigns weight to each byte (feature) in a fragment (sample). With these significant differences and approaches, SIFT produces promising (better) results compared to other works.

articleTitle: Improving Prospective Healthcare Outcomes by Leveraging Open Data and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare can improve diagnosis and clinical workflows, advancing standards and improving outcomes. AI for healthcare raises significant ethical and legal challenges. AI model development and deployment require transparency and interpretability. Transparency is the capacity to comprehend how an AI model makes recommendations, whereas interpretability is the ability to understand why. One such issue is the lack of transparency and interpretability of AI models, which might lead to a lack of trust in its decisions. Explainable AI (XAI) is an emerging research field that tries to solve this problem by creating AI models that can explain their recommendations. AI models need enough data to be accurate and reliable, thus they must be trained on various and extensive data sets. Open data and data sets (ODDS) can aid AI model development and training. Medical images, lab reports, and patient data are used to train algorithms to identify trends and make predictions in healthcare. Open data can help XAI in healthcare to enable AI models to be transparent, accountable, and interpretable. Open data makes possible AI model validation and replication. This is especially crucial in healthcare, where AI model flaws or biases can have serious implications. This paper discusses the use of ODDS and XAI to improve healthcare. ODDS's capability to promote trust and openness and best practices for using XAI in healthcare are also explored. The benefits and challenges of employing XAI and ODDS in their current forms are also discussed.

articleTitle: DTBAPred: Improved Prediction Drug-Target Binding Affinity using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Drugs are small molecules that usually bind with proteins, also called target, to control the cellular process of target in combatting disease associated with target (s). Effectiveness of a drug hugely depends upon the strength of its binding affinity with its partner proteins. As drug discovery is a lengthy and expensive process, in silico drug discovery and drug repurposing is an alternative complementary avenue for the researchers. Nowadays drug-target binding affinity (DTBA) prediction is a part and parcel of in any in silico drug discovery and drug repurposing process. There exist many precedents in the literature which considered machine learning (ML) based approach to predict DTBA. In the present article, we proposed a novel combination of features to represent drugs, targets, and feed into ML model to predict the DTBA. The proposed CatBoost based model DTBAPred outperformed the state-of-the-art traditional ML based methods in DAVIS benchmark dataset with 0.276 MSE, 0.579 R-square, and 0.866 CI. We considered two different fingerprints i.e., SMILES and Morgan to represent drugs; and SMILES fingerprint-based model showed better performance than Morgan fingerprint-based model, emphasizing that different fingerprints may also impact the DTBA prediction results. In summary obtained results indicate the superiority of the proposed method over existing traditional feature-based ML models for the same purpose and emphasized the incorporation of different fingerprints in the model. We believe, our proposed method will support to improve the DTBA prediction and escalate the drug discovery process.

articleTitle: Business Intelligence Implementation Obstacles in Saudi Public Universities
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Business Intelligence (BI) is a powerful tool that integrates systems and processes to extract data from diverse sources, encompassing vast datasets in various formats. Its purpose is to present meaningful information through multiple platforms, employing meticulously designed dashboards. Previous research has revealed that organizations often embark on large-scale BI integration; however, the failure rate in meeting expectations surpasses 70%. Consequently, this study aims to uncover the obstacles and related issues pertaining to BI implementation at the organizational level within Selected Saudi Public Universities (SSPUs) that have been practicing BI since 2018. Employing a qualitative approach, the study utilizes semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) to collect data. The collected textual data is thematically analyzed using a reflexive thematic analysis approach and NVivo software. The findings indicate that SSPUs follow a unified process comprising various implementation stages. The main themes within this process encompass the pre-implementation of BI, the implementation itself, the consequences of BI implementation, and the barriers encountered during implementation. This study contributes to the existing body of knowledge by providing comprehensive insights into BI implementation obstacles, specifically within SSPUs and, more broadly, within the mainstream of Saudi public universities. Additionally, it offers a roadmap for higher education institutions, enabling them to tailor their services and enhance revenue generation in alignment with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030.

articleTitle: A Dorsal Hand Vein Recognition System based on Various Machine and Deep Learning Classification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Dorsal vein biometrics is a widely used type of biometric identification due to the distinctiveness of the vein patterns, even between the right and left hands of the same person. In this study, a recognition system for human dorsal hand veins was proposed, utilizing various machine and deep learning methods such as KNN, SVM, DT, RF, and CNN on two hand dorsal vein datasets. The system demonstrated commendable performance on both datasets, achieving accuracy rates of 99.3%, 96%, 91.4%, 97.7%, and 99.8% for KNN, SVM, DT, RF, and CNN, respectively, even with the augmented dataset. However, the KNN and CNN models were found to be the most effective, producing high F1-scores, accuracy, and recall.

articleTitle: An Investigation of the Most Effective Ways for Cluster Sensors to Save Energy in Underwater Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Submarine WSNs are currently engaged in extensive research in a new setting for the benefit of people. UWSNs are regarded as one of the fastest-growing technical domains due to the many advantages of their application, like wildfire, healthcare, etc. UWSNs rely on the acoustic link as a means of communication and are comprised of low-power underwater sensors. Opportunities for underwater research utilizing sensors of varying depths have arisen thanks to recent technological developments. However, this article outlines the essential requirements of UWSNs to achieve essential services. With the advancement of underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs), various nautical activities may be carried out with remarkable efficiency. High propagation latency, high energy consumption, poor bandwidth, and low throughput are all characteristics of the routing protocols used in UWSNs, which constitute a significant drawback compared to their terrestrial counterparts. Unattended wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) can be set up in inaccessible places yet function normally. The batteries used by most sensors are extremely power-hungry and hard to swap out. Uneven use of energy resources is a significant barrier in UWSNs because it reduces network lifespan. To solve these issues, a routing method that conserves energy is required. The majority of these efforts have focused on developing energy-efficient routing protocols that can swiftly and reliably transport data packets from their point of origin to their final destination. This study analyzes and compares the many energy-efficient routing protocols that may be used in UWSNs, classifying them into a new taxonomy. Finally, we outline several unanswered questions and obstacles for further study.

articleTitle: A Model of Factors Influencing the Adoption and Utilization of E-Government Services in KSA (MFIAUEGS)
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This research demonstrates a proposal for a model of factors influencing the adoption and utilization of e-government services in Saudi Arabia (MIFEGSAU). This model was developed by combining factors from different well-known models and theories along with technical factors within the Technology Acceptance Model. This research focused on understanding and analyzing the factors taking e-government acceptance and implementation among all public members, particularly those with visual impairments. By Integrating motivational and technological factors recognized in the literature, hypotheses have been created to be studied and tested with Saudi citizens through a questionnaire survey and interviews.

articleTitle: Video Summarization Using Deep 3D ConvNets with Multi-Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method for key-shots-based video summarization by introducing 3D Convnets with Multi-Attention. The process starts by encoding the video data into time-variant frames in 3D followed by two steps of visual attention. The first step learns attention weights for features inside each frame and the second step learns attention weights for all the frames hence deciding the importance score between 0 and 1 for each frame for the target summarization. The current state-of-the-art method used 2D Convnets with self-attention hence losing the dependency of each frame on the next which results in self-attention focusing on fewer features. The keyframes and their relation with time are not maintained. The experimental studies evaluating the proposed approach on two standard video summarization datasets (i) SumMe and (ii) TVSum produced significant improvements. We report new state-of-the-art for the task of video summarization on these datasets.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Requirement Specification Framework for IoT-enabled Intelligent Transportation Systems using Unified Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The primary aim of IoT-enabled intelligent transportation is to administer and resolve the issues people confront for the improved transportation system. Technological advancement is an emerging domain because it reduces transportation challenges and makes machine-to-machine communication rapid and easy. The recent expansion in the IoT field provides a significant production perspective during a requirement specification. The existing requirement specification practices of IoT-enabled intelligent transportation systems must be utilized intelligently to comply with the challenges. To overcome these challenging problems, this article presents an inclusive survey of the difficulties relating to the requirements specifications of IoT-enabled transportation systems. The challenges of IoT-enabled intelligent transportation systems in the context of requirements specifications are assessed using specific evaluation criteria (e.g., parameters). This article proposes a clear enhanced framework for the specification of IoT-enabled intelligent transportation systems using a unified approach that extends our previous system. Initially, we reviewed the existing requirement specification work, identified and recognized the challenges, and highlighted how to deal with the difficulties in developing IoT-enabled intelligent transportation systems. The proposed framework is based on integrating proven techniques reported for similar applications. The prosed framework is applied to a specific case study of transportation systems. Moreover, a simple comparative analysis is also carried out based on identified evaluation parameters.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based System for Predicting Hypertension in North Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study presents a machine learning-based (ML) System made to predict hypertension in people living in northern Saudi Arabia. People in the area provided a sizable dataset of some medical information, lifestyle choices, and other pertinent information. To identify the main risk factors for hypertension, the data was used to train a machine learning model. The ML-based system was found to be highly accurate in predicting hypertension, and it can be easily accessed by medical professionals by being integrated into current medical systems. In order to provide targeted screenings and interventions, the system can also be used to identify people who are at a high risk of developing hypertension. This ML-based system may enhance early detection and treatment of hypertension in the community of northern Saudi Arabia, improving, therefore, health outcomes.

articleTitle: OKAZ: A Deep-learning-Based System for Automatic Arabic Poem Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: A poem is a sequence of verses that conveys emotions and views via an in-depth knowledge of a language. It represents a deeply rooted element of any language's cultural heritage. For decades, poem generation has been limited to human experts with considerable talent and linguistic skills. However, researchers have been attracted to this area lately, investigating the possibilities of auto-generating poems using AI-based systems. They observe considerable success with highly-inflected languages like Chinese. Nevertheless, research on the auto-generation of Arabic poems is sparse. This work presents one of the first attempts to address this research problem for Arabic poetry by exploring the effectiveness of using deep learning-based models to generate Arabic verses. Our findings show that GPT-2 was able to achieve the best results by outperforming other models and attaining a BLEU score of 0.082 and an average performance of 2.94 out of 5 when evaluated by human experts. We believe that these findings reveal the need for further investigations to bridge the performance gap when compared to the average human-level performance score of 4.62.

articleTitle: Improved Parallel k-means Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The K-means algorithm, one of the most well-known clustering techniques, has been widely employed to solve a variety of problems. In contrast, the k-means clustering algorithm has numerous restrictions. For instance, the difficulty of dealing with voluminous data, the sensitivity of the outlier, and the random selection of the initial centroid. In this paper, a parallel K-means clustering algorithm is proposed that improves the performance of sequential K-means clustering algorithms by removing outliers from the data before clustering, dividing the data into smaller sections among the threads, and selecting the initial centroid with care. Our primary parallelization tool was OpenMP, which was implemented using the C programming language on 234,296 records. This experiment was conducted using sequential and parallel source code, with modifications made to enhance the parallel functionality. The improved parallel execution resulted in a significant reduction in execution time relative to sequential algorithms. The proposed algorithm source code is also available on GitHub for the community.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Federated Learning Towards Big data IoT with Future Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Over the past few years, big data has come a long way, allowing us to make sense of the immense amounts of information being produced by cutting-edge services and apps, as well as a plethora of IoT devices. Only through extracting value from huge data through data analytics can big data's full potential be accomplished [6]. Machine learning (ML) plays a highly essential part in this process because of its capacity to know patterns and then deliver insights through learning from facts. Since the data may include private information about individuals, governments, or financial accounts, using a more traditional technique raises serious concerns about data confidentiality. Recently, Federated learning (FL) seemed like a potential learning procedure that could help us get beyond this obstacle. In FL, the central ML algorithm is only given the parameters from the local devices so that it can train and make predictions on a global scale. The aforementioned problems with huge data may be amenable to resolution thanks to this aspect of FL. Furthermore, a thorough assessment of FL for big data applications has forward done, leaving a void in the literature. This article delivers a summary of FL, big data, and the motives for the procedure of FL for big data by surveying its use in big data applications. In particular, it is important to thoroughly examine the usage of FL for major big data services with applications like the smart city, remote surgery, transportation, smart grid, and social networks. Additionally, briefly discuss the most pressing problems associated with this engaging subject and the most potential approaches to fixing them.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis on Machine Learning and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network to Predict Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) established on machine learning (ML) techniques have been used in intelligence investigation, food safety, biological recognition, and material study. However, ML techniques typically require additional preprocessing or attribute engineering, and conducting large data employing these techniques is problematic. Deep Learning (DL) techniques involve minimal input data by analyzing every probable attribute established in the network. Therefore, this study employed ML techniques. These are K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Naïve Bayes (NB) Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Decision Trees (DT). Then, the result is compared with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network structure (1D-CNN). In this research, we utilize Rhodamine 6G (R6G) as an objective molecule. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the 1D-CNN offered.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Saudi Kindergarten Teachers’ Attitudes towards and Uses of Technology as Literacy Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Although many studies have examined how computer technology affects young children's education, relatively few, especially in Saudi Arabia, have examined the critical role instructors play in successfully integrating technology into early education. The COVID-19 pandemic has caused a paradigm change, making it very important to employ technology in education, especially in schools. We give a statistical analysis of teachers' viewpoints on using technology in the classroom in this research. The main goal of this study is to evaluate the importance of employing technology in education. The trial was carried out using two fundamental techniques, namely surveys, and interviews. The tools were used to gather data from 470 respondents. We analyzed the gathered data set using the SPSSS program and associated libraries. The favorable attitude about utilizing technology as a literacy aid was shown by interesting data. The management of the school and the government might benefit from using technology as a literacy tool. The report also identifies certain obstacles to employing technology, such as time constraints and instructors' lack of technological expertise. Ultimately, this study's findings point to the significance of teacher training in technology utilization. Consequently, a well-designed strategy outlining the educational objectives that may be achieved by using technology is required for technology to be effectively introduced into kindergartens.

articleTitle: Review the Recent IoT systems for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has played significant rule in the health care domain recently, from mentoring patients remotely to offering many remote alarm functions. In general, the IoT has been employed in the medical devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucose meter, and heart rate devices as examples) for the purpose of monitoring and recording the patient’s vital signs. This allows healthcare providers to remotely gather health information and then apply decision support rules, in order to allow early intervention in the treatment process. However, there are numerous issues in the healthcare delivery, technology development, role of government, and behaviour and the acceptance by medical doctors and hospitals. This paper presents a review of the emergence of the IoT technology in the health care applications, and investigates the impact of adopting IoT technology in the health care field. In addition, we surveyed, analyzed, and discussed the recent practical developed IoT-based healthcare systems. Moreover, this paper discusses and analyses the success of the recent developed IoT-based approaches in the domain of healthcare.

articleTitle: An analytical Study of Mobile Applications Recommended by The Ministry of Hajj and Umrah
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Every year, millions of Muslims visit Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Hajj, a religious pilgrimage. To help pilgrims overcome potential challenges, several public and private organizations offer a range of services and facilities. Technology has acquired growing attention as a key tool for offering services, particularly modern technology used to deliver varied services includes mobile applications (apps). Various organizations have created Islamic applications for smart mobile devices to help pilgrims conveniently carry out their Islamic rites. This work analyzes and reviews all Hajj and Umrah mobile applications developed or recommended by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. Furthermore, difficulties and limitations in these applications are discussed, and new solutions are recommended to address them. The results show that the average software size is 72.08 MB, and the total size of all the programs under analysis is 937.1 MB. To this end, this research examines how many languages were used in various applications. It turns out that English continues to be the most often used language in apps, with a usage rate of 100%, followed by Arabic (91.67%), Urdu (50%), and French (50%). Turjuman has the most language options, with 25 supported languages.

articleTitle: Data Privacy and Security Model in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The privacy and security of data stored in cloud environments remain a significant challenge for organizations and individual users. Since data is stored in different physical locations, data security and privacy are particularly critical in cloud environments. Today, data privacy and security are the main concerns of governments, organizations, academics, and IT industry experts. The future development of cloud computing depends on providing reliable data privacy and security solutions. The current study performs an in-depth assessment of data privacy and security issues affecting individual users and organizations. The analysis is followed up by a suggested solution of an adequate data security and privacy model based on a combination of file encryption and service fragmentation. Specifically, the development of the analysis and security model focuses on the Linux operating system. Finally, extensive simulation results prove that the proposed model gives more privacy accuracy and reliability in cloud environments.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Conceptual Model for Scrum Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Scrum is an incremental, interactive agile framework widely used to develop practical problems; the Scrum team focuses on achieving a common goal each cycle, "Sprint Goal" instead of the traditional sequential technique for delivering products. Although many organizations are adopting Scrum, it is still following the traditional manual approaches. Even though many tools are available in the market to facilitate project management and Scrum master tasks, the support is still limited and lacks the utilization of Artificial Intelligence science. This study focuses on integrating the Scrum framework with Artificial Intelligence to build a predicting model that can assist project management "in particular the Scrum master" to predict the achievement of the Scrum Team per Sprint using Story Points; this prediction is built based on several factors that can affect the burndown charts per Sprint.

articleTitle: LiFi in Short-Range Wireless Communication of IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the new era, various communication systems rapidly evolve to pertain the user's needs. One of these emerging communication systems, which is crucial to providing better life aspects, is the Internet of Things (IoT). Communications between the devices in the IoT is the core part of the system. There are two types of communication between the devices in the IoT; short-range wireless communication and long-range wired or wireless communication. This paper is dedicated to discuss the short-range wireless communication in the IoT. These are not to limit but short-range wireless communication includes Bluetooth, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Wireless-Fidelity (WiFi), Light-Fidelity (LiFi), Radio-frequency Identification (RFID), or ZigBee. This paper addresses the LiFi short-range wireless communication system from the operations, modulation techniques, and IEEE 802.15.7 layer architecture. Finally, a comparison of these short-range wireless communications has been made to comprehend their importance in the life of the IoT.

articleTitle: Investigating and developing a model of factors influencing the adoption and utilization of e-government services in KSA
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: E-Government raises the clarity by using Information Communication Technologies (ICTs) as utilization tool for providing public services. In addition, E-government is ICT communication tool between the citizens and government sectors with the purpose of focusing on efficiency, transparency, and effectiveness. The goal of this research is to create, refine and validate a model of factors influencing the adoption and utilization of e-Government services in KSA (MFIAUEGS). To achieve our aim, we combined factors from different well-known models and theories along with motivational and technical factors within the Technology Acceptance Model. This study analyzes and investigates the factors taking e-Government acceptance and implementation among all public members, particularly those with visual impairments. Through a pilot study which supports the successful implementation of governmental systems in Saudi Arabia, this research promises to reveal invaluable insights into how to use technology for maximal benefit. The findings show that 29 items are reliable and valid within the scope of our research, with a strong positive correlation. As a methodology, the proposed model has been constructed from different high reliable models, then factors have been added to the proposed model. Finally, the proposed model has been validated by the associated stakeholders using a questionnaire tool. The research tool was a survey using a 31-item questionnaire distributed to 28 Saudi citizens. SPSS has been used to analyze and test the factor items studied in this research.

articleTitle: What to predict from Twitter Data?
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the last decade, Twitter data has become one of the most valuable research sources for many areas including health, marketing, security, and politics. Researchers prefer Twitter data since it is completely public and can be easily downloaded using Twitter APIs. The recent intensive use of Twitter data makes it difficult for researchers to follow or analyze its research. In this paper, we summarize most of the predictable patterns, aspects, and attitudes from Twitter data and analyze the performance and feasibility of the algorithms used. Moreover, we describe the current popular Twitter datasets used in various domains and applications. Current challenges and research gaps are discussed, and some recommendations are given for future works from different perspectives.
